Package com.yetnt.utils.builders

Class InlineHTML

java.lang.Object
com.yetnt.utils.builders.InlineHTML
public class InlineHTML extends Object
The most important class that helps me avoid learning the pain that is JFormattedTextField

InlineHTML is a utility class designed to simplify the creation of rich text content for JLabels. It provides methods for applying various HTML-like formatting, such as bold, italic, underline, font colour, font size, and paragraph wrapping, without directly manipulating raw HTML strings.

The class internally manages a list of opening and closing HTML tags, which are applied to the content when toString() or wrapHTML() is called. This allows for method chaining to build complex formatted text efficiently.

Example usage: 


     InlineHTML richText = new InlineHTML("Hello, World!")
         .bold()                              // wraps in <b></b> tag
         .font(Color.BLUE)                    // wraps in <font color="#0000FF"></font>
         .paragraph();                        // wraps in <p></p>
     myLabel.setText(richText.wrapHTML());    // finally wraps in <html></html>

    • addAttributes

      public InlineHTML addAttributes(LinkedHashMap<String,String> attributes)
      Adds attributes to the most recently opened HTML tag. This method is useful for dynamically adding properties like id, class, or other custom attributes to a tag that has just been opened using methods like wrapTag().

      The attributes are appended to the last tag added to the open list.

      Parameters:
      attributes - A LinkedHashMap where keys are attribute names and values are attribute values.
      Returns:
      The current InlineHTML instance for method chaining.

    • addStyle

      public InlineHTML addStyle(LinkedHashMap<String,String> style)
      Adds inline CSS styles to the most recently opened HTML tag. This method allows for dynamic application of CSS properties to a tag that has just been opened. It checks if a 'style' attribute already exists on the last opened tag and throws a RuntimeException if it does, to prevent overwriting.

      The styles are formatted into a CSS string and then added as a 'style' attribute.

      Parameters:
      style - A LinkedHashMap where keys are CSS property names and values are their corresponding values.
      Returns:
      The current InlineHTML instance for method chaining.

    • wrapTag

      public InlineHTML wrapTag(String tag, LinkedHashMap<String,String> attributes)
      Wraps the content with a generic HTML tag, applying specified attributes. This method is used internally by other formatting methods like bold(), italic(), and font().
      Parameters:
      tag - The HTML tag name (e.g., "b", "i", "font").
      attributes - A LinkedHashMap of attribute names and their values (e.g., "color" -> "#FF0000").
      Returns:
      The current InlineHTML instance for method chaining.

    • wrapTag

      public InlineHTML wrapTag(String tag, LinkedHashMap<String,String> attributes, LinkedHashMap<String,String> style)
      Wraps the content with a generic HTML tag, applying specified attributes and inline styles. This method allows for more complex styling than wrapTag(String, LinkedHashMap).
      Parameters:
      tag - The HTML tag name (e.g., "div", "span").
      attributes - A LinkedHashMap of attribute names and their values (e.g., "id" -> "myDiv").
      style - A LinkedHashMap of CSS style properties and their values (e.g., "color" -> "red", "font-size" -> "12px").
      Returns:
      The current InlineHTML instance for method chaining.

    • wrapUsing

      public InlineHTML wrapUsing(InlineHTML other)
      Applies the opening and closing tags from another InlineHTML instance to the current instance. The tags from other are added before the current instance's own tags, effectively wrapping the current instance's content and styling.
      Parameters:
      other - The InlineHTML instance whose tags are to be applied.
      Returns:
      The current InlineHTML instance for method chaining.
